raw.assessment: The incumbent directly previews embedded captions in the required delivery format and retains earlier previews. It reached the intended preview within 15 minutes in 20/30 sessions. Repeated saves, variable render times and completion inversions could jointly create waiting and identification work, but their causal contributions are unmeasured. H1-O4 establishes expectation mismatches, including one previous video cut; it does not locate the fault in selection, input binding or rendering. H1-O7 limits any claim that full rendering inherently prevents timely, unambiguous previews: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in five to 11 minutes. The 49-hour sampled week does not establish festival capacity.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind each request to retained, immutable video and caption revisions, carry their hashes through rendering, and display that pairing consistently on the completed preview and download.
openings.delta: Replace reliance on separately named captions and completion-numbered previews with an inspectable intended pair; retain a pinned last-delivered pair and its original captions.
openings.prediction: When jobs finish out of order or sources change during rendering, outputs still match their recorded requested pair and editors identify the intended pair more reliably.
openings.probe: In private staging, use fabricated footage to interleave two video cuts and caption revisions, including delayed jobs and edits after submission. Compare requested and output hashes and have both editors select the final intended pair. Verify the previous delivery remains retrievable with its original wording.
assumptions: Revision retention and request metadata can be added within four engineer-days and one editor-day.
The current worker can consume fixed revisions within the existing processing allowance.
Clear pairing labels are understandable to editors.

openings.claim: Does excess time after the final edit primarily precede availability of the correct preview or follow its availability?
openings.delta: Distinguish processing delay from locating and checking an already available result before choosing further changes.
openings.prediction: A processing explanation predicts most excess time occurs before correct-output availability; an identification explanation predicts it occurs afterward. Mixed intervals would support a combined account.
openings.probe: Use existing render timestamps and brief staged replays with both editors to record final save, correct-output availability, first correct selection and confirmation. Include single-correction and repeated-save histories; separate watching time from selection time and record incorrect choices.
assumptions: A small replay sample fits the shared editor-day and remaining engineering allowance.
Staged behavior is informative but requires confirmation in the 30 new sessions.

raw.assessment: The observations establish delay and version mismatch, but do not identify their causes. These are candidate openings; neither establishes the 30-session success target or festival capacity.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a caption audition mode could replay only changed cues with surrounding video, applying timed captions in the browser from private storage. Editors could inspect wording and timing immediately, then request the existing embedded-caption render for delivery.
openings.delta: Make the edited cue, rather than a newly rendered whole video, the immediate unit of inspection. Bind each audition and subsequent render to an immutable video/caption pair; retain the last delivered pair and original text.
openings.prediction: Correction sessions need fewer full renders while editors still detect planted wording and timing errors; browser and embedded previews agree on those judgments.
openings.probe: Timebox a staging prototype using demonstration footage. Have both editors assess planted errors through cue auditions and embedded previews. Measure disagreement, correctly identified preview time, processing hours, and engineering effort before testing 30 new sessions.
assumptions: Existing private infrastructure supports the audition within four engineer-days and one editor-day.
Cue context and browser timing are adequate for the edits tested; full embedded preview remains available where they are inadequate.

openings.claim: Does returning after an interruption erase the editor's remembered target, even when every preview is accurately labeled?
openings.delta: Test continuity of intent as a separate source of uncertainty: a persistent receipt records the selected video cut and a distinctive final caption excerpt before the editor leaves.
openings.prediction: With render waits, labels, and completion order held constant, interruption increases selection errors or selection time; the receipt selectively reduces that interruption penalty.
openings.probe: Use counterbalanced fabricated staging tasks crossing interruption/no interruption with receipt/no receipt. Log waiting and selection separately, and check selected pairs against the stipulated target. An absent interaction weakens this explanation.
assumptions: A small demonstration task set fits the shared editor-day budget; two editors provide exploratory evidence only.

openings.claim: Bind immutable video/caption revisions through request, render and download; display the pair and pin last delivery with original wording.
openings.discriminator: Outputs match requested hashes despite edits and completion inversions; editors identify intended pairs.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints, conditional on budget feasibility.
openings.probe: Interleave cuts, captions, delayed jobs and post-submission edits in staging; compare hashes, editor selections and prior-delivery retrieval.
openings.uncertainty: Mismatch origin, label comprehension and implementation cost remain unknown.

openings.claim: Separate delay before correct-output availability from subsequent identification and watching.
openings.discriminator: Excess time before versus after availability distinguishes processing, identification or mixed causes.
openings.probe: Replay single-correction and repeated-save histories; timestamp final save, availability, selection and confirmation, separating watching and errors.
openings.uncertainty: Small staged samples need confirmation; nine successful correction sessions limit blanket rendering claims.

openings.claim: Audition changed timed cues with surrounding video in-browser; bind immutable pairs and retain embedded delivery rendering.
openings.discriminator: Fewer full renders with comparable detection of planted wording/timing errors.
openings.fit: Uncertain feasibility; retain private processing, previous delivery and full preview fallback.
openings.probe: Timebox prototype; compare audition/embedded judgments, identification time, processing and engineering effort.
openings.uncertainty: Cue context, browser timing and four-day feasibility unproven.

openings.claim: Interruptions may erase remembered intent despite accurate labels; a persistent cut/caption-excerpt receipt may restore it.
openings.discriminator: Receipt selectively reduces interruption-related selection errors or time with waits, labels and order fixed.
openings.probe: Counterbalance interruption and receipt in fabricated tasks; check selected pairs and separate waiting/selection.
openings.uncertainty: Absent interaction weakens explanation; two editors provide exploratory evidence.

post_distill.decision: Stage probes on existing private accounts within four engineer-days, one editor-day and 80 hours/week collectively. Synthetic evidence proves no outcome: confirm >=27/30 within 15 minutes and zero unintended delivered pairs. Festival capacity remains unknown.
